reason: Use Tier 2: replace uniform graph-depth averaging with jointly learned node-adaptive depth attention. Collaborative propagation and supervised-edge masking improved validation, whereas increasing negatives and adding recent-query complexity did not; this suggests testing the graph representation rather than extending history attention again. Uniform averaging forces every user and item to share the same neighborhood depth, potentially smoothing sparse or specialized preferences excessively, although the observed plateau does not establish that cause.

plan.model_design: In GraphRecommender._propagate(adjacency), retain embeddings from depths zero through self.layers and replace their arithmetic mean with node-adaptive attention across those depths, a Tier 2 representation change. Implement one shared scorer s_k = Linear(tanh(Linear(concat(x_0, x_k)))) and compute result = sum_k softmax(s)_k * x_k, zero-initializing the final scoring layer so aggregation initially equals the existing uniform average; initialize the new module after existing modules to preserve their initialization sequence. This lets the single network learn when direct preferences or broader collaborative neighborhoods are useful without adding independently fitted predictors. Preserve existing variable names, constructor positional arguments, _propagate, propagate, forward, predict_indices, and predict_history signatures, and apply the identical aggregation to temporary masked training graphs and the full training graph used for inference. Keep all current history modules, tied embeddings, item bias, supervised-edge masking, sampled-softmax loss, regularization, and hyperparameters unchanged to isolate graph-depth aggregation.
